scope.covers: the 24 CONFIRMED findings of the independent adversarial review wf_a6b49ecf-667 (2026-08-12), which is the population criterion 2 names
scope.excludes: the 2026-08-06 guards review (42 severity-tagged rows: 10 HIGH, 26 MEDIUM, 6 LOW) and the R1/R2 AR-series
scope.exclusion_basis: CLOSED DECISION in coverage_ledger_2026-08-09.md: guards that can be silently DISARMED BY EDITING UNBLUFF'S OWN SOURCE are WON'T-FIX, which deletes AR-1..AR-11 and the 32 AR MEDIUM/LOW rows from the roadmap entirely. The ONLY way any returns is if criterion 1 finds a README claim depending on it.
scope.note: A PASS here is a PASS over `covers`, never over the whole review history. Stated in the DATA so the gate cannot imply coverage it does not have.

findings.name: FTB-RC4
findings.finding: C1 is FALSE: pytest rc 4 is what a BROKEN conftest.py returns, so the waiver silently disables the gate on the user's own broken code

findings.name: FTB-MASK
findings.finding: Containment notice is once-per-project FOREVER, so a permanently-inconclusive repo ends every turn after the first with rc 0 and EMPTY stderr

findings.name: FTB-RC4-dup
findings.finding: C1 is FALSE for rc 4: a broken conftest.py is the user's own code, and after one notice the gate is silent forever

findings.name: FTB-MASK-key
findings.finding: The inconclusive notice is keyed by path hash alone, so a LATER, DIFFERENT nothing-verified state is permanently silent - exit 0, empty stderr, byte-identical to a green turn

findings.name: FTB-MASK-nogate
findings.finding: _notice_no_gate has two different reasons sharing ONE state key, so the "add a gate" notice permanently masks the "pytest is not importable" notice - the exact masking _inconclusive_state_path's docstring forbids

findings.name: ROSTER-DERIVE
findings.finding: Section N's "the roster is now the AST import closure of the wired entry points" is false - 7 of 25 hooks reach it only via a hardcoded REQUIRED_HOOKS tuple, and dispatcher-roster drift is silent end to end

findings.name: REVIEWRUNS-GAP
findings.finding: review_runs.json omits the entire 2026-08-06 guards run (42 confirmed, 10 HIGH), so the ledger's "the 42 is the complete population" closure is complete only over what was recorded

findings.name: FTB-C4
findings.finding: C4 is FALSE after the first turn: the inconclusive notice is once-per-PROJECT and keyed only by cwd, so later turns - and later, different reasons - are byte-identical to a green run

findings.name: RC3-BLOCKS
findings.finding: The exit map is incomplete in the blocking direction: ExitCode.INTERNAL_ERROR (3) is by pytest's own definition not a verdict, and still hard-blocks the turn end and the push

findings.name: FTB-CFG
findings.finding: C3 false negative from a canonical-value gap: _PYTEST_CONFIG_MARKERS recognises 4 of pytest's 7 config filenames, so real pytest projects get no gate

findings.name: FTB-SPELL
findings.finding: _is_pytest_command misses `py.test` and `pytest-3`, so the FASTTEST-BLOCK hard block survives verbatim for those spellings in BOTH gates

findings.name: FTB-LAYOUT
findings.finding: C3 is false: looks_like_pytest_project rejects three of the most common genuine pytest layouts, and README claims 'auto-detects pytest'

findings.name: FTB-CAP
findings.finding: _PYTEST_FILE_CAP counts every file, so a tests/ tree with >5000 non-Python fixtures and ZERO .py files is classified as a pytest project

findings.name: FTB-MARKER
findings.finding: _has_pytest_config matches its markers inside comments and strings, and reads config without utf-8-sig while _read_override uses it

findings.name: FTB-SPELL-pytest
findings.finding: `py.test` - pytest's own still-shipped console script - is not recognised, so FASTTEST-BLOCK survives verbatim for that spelling

findings.name: FTB-C2-CONTROLS
findings.finding: The C2 control loop is decorative: none of its three commands contains the substring 'pytest', so a substring match passes it

findings.name: FTB-GATES
findings.finding: The two gates DISAGREE about a real pytest project whose pytest is not importable: the Stop gate names the reason, the push gate says "has no test command - nothing to verify"

findings.name: STALE-DOCSTRINGS
findings.finding: Stale detection claims the fix did not update: fast_test_on_stop's own module docstring, pre_push_gate's docstring, the repo's .claude/fast-test.cmd comment, and a CHANGELOG with no entry for the behaviour change

findings.name: C2-FALSE
findings.finding: Design claim C2 is false: _is_pytest_command misclassifies non-pytest commands, and the repo's own push-gate selftest is built on that misclassification

findings.name: WT-CAUSE
findings.finding: A failing `git commit` is misreported as "git worktree unavailable", silently drops worktree-delegation (and scenarios 17+18) from the denominator, and the suite still exits 0

findings.name: SH-CONTRADICTORY
findings.finding: `_sh_delegation_fails` can emit three mutually contradictory statements in one run, and the probe asserts only the verdict and the numerator - never the message

findings.name: OPEN-COUNT-ZERO
findings.finding: _open_count() maps an ABSENT `open` field to 0, and 45 of 68 ledger entries have no such field - the ledger reads unknown as zero

findings.name: MARKER-UNPINNED
findings.finding: _has_pytest_config's marker check is unpinned - dropping it re-introduces FASTTEST-BLOCK on every Python repo and the suite stays green

findings.name: CAP-UNPINNED
findings.finding: The three-state cap in _has_collectible_tests is unpinned; collapsing None to False silently disables the gate on any large tests/ tree
